brief:
I want to keep my robot arm's motor coolant loop separate from the lab chiller with a printed
water-to-water heat exchanger: a counterflow dual-gyroid block, PETG on an FDM printer, standing on its
100 x 60 face. It must fit in a 100 x 60 x 50 mm box (x along the 100 mm length, y across the 60, z up,
origin at a bottom corner). Chiller water comes in at the x = 0 end and leaves at the x = 100 end; the
arm's loop goes in and out through the two long sides (y = 0 and y = 60), running against the chiller
water. Flows: chiller 1.5 L/min at 15 C, arm loop 1 L/min at 45 C. It has to move at least 150 W out of
the arm's loop, and neither side may lose more than 0.1 bar. I'm using 6 mm hose barbs, so give every
port at least a 5 mm bore.
